content.thinking:
I'm planning a humanoid medic character with clean Overwatch-style shapes, roughly 1.8m tall, using a white/charcoal palette with a glowing teal-green accent color.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure—hips, spine chain with multiple joints, neck, and head—figuring out how the joint names and chain spans map to actual bone positions and orientations.

For the jaw I'm placing a joint parented to the head with an aim direction, then building a lower jaw part rigidly attached to it. For the arms, I'm setting shoulder joints symmetrically on each side and computing elbow and wrist positions using an A-pose angle, working out the trigonometry to get upper arm and forearm lengths right.

Continuing the arm chain, I'm computing elbow and wrist coordinates by stepping along the A-pose angle, then deciding the chain should have four named points (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) so the final segment ends at the hand tip, using a polyline for the joint path and L/R suffixes based on the side sign.

Now I'm sketching helper functions: a sweep-based rod with tapered radii and smooth caps for the arm, choosing sides count for a slightly faceted but mostly smooth Overwatch-style look, and a box helper for armor pieces attached to bones.

For the key armor plates (chest, shoulder pads, shin guards), I plan to use extruded shapes with bevels instead of plain boxes to get that stylized rounded-plate look, being careful with convex outlines and smoothing settings to avoid self-intersection issues. For hands, I'm considering simple capsule fingers versus building a full finger joint chain for proper articulation.

Working out finger positioning and joint budget...

For the design, I'm thinking cyborg-style arms: left arm mechanical with dark segments and glowing rings, right arm with armored sleeve, plus a cyber eye or visor glow on the face and some kind of hood or medic-style headgear.

For the head, I'm planning a skin-toned sphere with one half as a cyber plate with a glowing eye, swept-back hair, and a headset with white ear cups and a mic boom. I'll use decals for facial features -- an organic eye on one side (white, brown iris, brow) and a glowing teal cyber-eye ring on the other, applied onto the head sphere surface.

Now I'm working out the leg skeleton, placing hip, knee, ankle, and toe joints as a chained path with specific coordinates so the foot points forward along the final tangent.

I'm planning to sweep the leg as a tube with tapering radius (thicker thigh, thinner shin), but only up to the ankle so the foot geometry stays as separate boot parts rather than part of the tube, keeping the sole resting at floor level.

Still placing torso stations...

For colors, I'm going for an Overwatch-style flat palette with subtle countershading paint on the suit, keeping panel lines and armor plates simple with white and teal trim rather than toon shading. I'm defining the color set now: whites, suit darks, grays, and metal tones.

I'm settling on a single teal accent rather than mixing in orange, skipping logos but allowing a generic plus-sign decal on the shoulder as a medic motif. Now I'm positioning the healing staff in the right hand, planted vertically beside the body near the wrist, working out the exact coordinates so it reads as upright and grounded.

Working out finger placement around the staff...

Still working out finger angles...

Repositioning the wrist and hand coordinates so the palm wraps the staff without clipping, and spacing finger joints along the staff's y-axis. The left arm will be mechanical, hanging naturally with metallic fingers, while the staff itself gets a dark gray shaft.

Now I'm designing the staff's head: a crystal cradle with a glowing teal orb and curved wing-like prongs, parented to the right hand's tip so it stays gripped while the ferrule touches the floor. I'll add a rotating torus ring around the orb for a floating glow effect.

For the back, I'm planning a medpack tank with glowing healing canisters and hoses sweeping to the hip, plus a chest cross-plate, shoulder pads, a pouch belt, a thigh injector holster, and a vial bandolier. I'll skip a full cape in favor of hip-mounted tabard flaps front and back, add a three-joint ponytail chain using a tail-type role, and include a headset with mic before moving into the head/face sculpting.

Now I'm working out the head sphere's position and scale against the neck joint to get overall character height right, settling around 1.85-1.9m including hair, then placing the boots at floor level and setting up the face decal with a scaled sphere geometry and cyber-style eye direction vectors.

I'm planning the eye decals: mirrored placement so the organic eye goes on the right side and the cyber eye on the left, with separate SVG textures for each—an organic eye with iris, pupil, highlight, brow, and lash, versus a cyber eye with a dark plate, teal iris ring, and crosshair detail, plus a matching cyber cheek plate.

Working out the sphere geometry parameters for the partial cheek plate...

I'll have the decal project onto both the head and plate surfaces so the eye texture reads correctly on the organic side. For the remaining features I'm adding a small nose wedge, a mouth line decal, ear spheres, and a hair cap built from a partial sphere shaped like bangs covering the front of the head.

I'm figuring out the right theta cutoff for the hairline so it sits above the eyes rather than covering them, testing elevation angles until the forehead coverage looks correct.

With the top and back cap angles settled, I'm planning the extruded bang tufts for swept fringe detail, plus a ponytail: a hairband joint at the back of the head with a three-segment chain sweeping downward and outward to form hanging hair strands.

Now I'm figuring out the joint hierarchy — fetching the head joint as the tip of the neck chain to parent the hair, then setting up the neck itself as a two-point sweep chain colored for skin, and continuing on to define the spine chain parented to the hips.

Working through the skeleton placement: hips at the root, spine joints stacking upward at increasing heights, with the torso loft spanning hips to spine, and the neck chain beginning right where the spine ends so the arms and head attach cleanly.

For the suit's look, I'm deciding on a flat dark base color with an accent, planning to add teal stripes along the sides of the torso using sweep sectors positioned around the tube's circumference.

Now I'm shifting to armor pieces, setting up a plate helper function and starting to sketch the chest plate's outline using a front-view coordinate system.

Working out the cross-emblem box dimensions and their z-offsets relative to the plate's front face, adjusting the plate's center depth so the cross sits slightly in front of the chest surface without clipping.

I'm also deciding which spine bone the plate should attach to since it spans the 1.20-1.48 region, and thinking through how to build the waist belt as a closed ring of swept points rather than relying on risky surface-loop methods.

For the belt, I'm sizing an ellipse around the torso with specific horizontal and vertical radii and a thin tube cross-section, picking dark brown/gray with a teal buckle, binding it to the hips bone, and wrapping it with a reusable ring-building helper function. Then I'm moving on to pelvis armor, sketching trapezoid-shaped white tassets positioned on the front thighs near the hip joint.

I'm now working out thigh armor: placing cylindrical rod segments along each thigh to match its natural taper, keying radius values at several points from hip to ankle (roughly .088 down to .046) so the armor smoothly follows the leg's sweep.

Next I'm sizing knee pads, shin guards, and checking that every guard radius stays slightly larger than the underlying limb's own radius at that height, verifying this against the sweep radius values along the shin down to the ankle.

I realize I should just build a shared leg path from hip to knee to ankle and reuse it for both the limb geometry and the guard placement, sampling points along the path by arc-length so the guards line up naturally with the leg's curve.

For the boots, I'm sketching a side-profile outline (heel, toe, ankle top) that I'll extrude sideways to give the foot some thickness, rather than modeling it as a simple box.

Still shaping boot geometry...

Adding a teal toe cap accent, then moving to arm armor: a suited upper arm with white armored rods and a large ellipsoid shoulder pauldron with a thin teal ring band for a bold Overwatch-style bevel.

For the left cyborg arm I'm building a reusable band helper that sweeps a closed ring perpendicular to an arbitrary axis direction, using cross-product math to find basis vectors -- this will generate forearm glow rings, bracelets, and staff bands all from one generic function.

Still mapping out joint coordinates...

Still working out arm guard placement...

The sweep chain for the arm covers three spans ending at the hand tip, then I need to add a palm box oriented to the wrist direction, with the thin dimension running sideways and the width running front-to-back so the palm faces the body correctly.

Now I'm working out the cyborg left hand: a dark metal palm block with fingers built as rod chains that curl slightly forward, starting from the palm center and offset along the hand direction toward the fingertip.

I'm working out where each finger starts relative to the hand position and figuring out its curl direction toward the palm, which means determining the perpendicular vector to the arm direction so the fingers bend toward the body naturally.

Writing finger segment coordinates...

Now I'm designing the backpack: a medpack box with a teal cross glow, two glowing canisters flanking it, and hoses curving down from the pack to a hip pouch using smooth catmull-rom paths.

I'm reconsidering shoulder-to-hip straps crossing the torso, but deciding to skip that and instead add a bandolier of vials around the left hip using a tilted ring whose radius is sized to clear the torso's elliptical cross-section.

Writing ellipse ring math...

I'm placing small teal-glow vial cylinders along the diagonal bandolier belt, keeping part count manageable within the 1000-part budget. Now I'm sketching out the staff dimensions, planning the shaft to run from the hand grip up past the head to a top around height 2.0.

Still writing staff geometry...

Still shaping the orb cradle...

Checking the remaining edges confirms the polygon stays simple with no unwanted crossings, so the outline works. Now I'm setting up the orb's extrusion parameters—position, thickness, and bevel—keeping smoothing at zero to avoid rendering issues, and working out the thickness vector from the cross product of the local axes.

Next I'm defining a staff joint attached to the hand, positioning it so it aligns with where the hand grips, checking that the forearm geometry doesn't collide with the staff's placement given the offsets in x and z.

Now I'm working out how the fingers should wrap around the staff's circumference, figuring out the angle where the palm meets the staff versus where the fingertips curl around the front.

Working out the thumb path wrapping the opposite side of the hand to meet the fingertips, then positioning the palm as a small box near the staff connecting to the wrist sweep endpoint.

I'm adjusting the palm position slightly to avoid overlap with the staff, adding a wrist cuff ring, and now sketching the headset — a curved band arcing over the top of the head between the ears with cylindrical ear cups at each side.

Now I'm adding a boom mic sweeping from the ear cup toward the mouth with a teal tip, setting up the jaw as a child joint of the head with a chin-shaped ellipsoid, and shaping the head itself as an ellipsoid whose lower portion forms the face.

I'm checking whether the chin sphere protrudes correctly past the head sphere's surface at jaw height, confirming the geometry sticks out enough to form a visible chin, then realizing a mouth decal won't bend properly across the rigid jaw piece, so I'm reconsidering placing the mouth line on the upper head instead.

Now I'm positioning the eyes on the head surface by computing the sphere's curvature at that height, figuring the nose as a small darker sphere protrusion, and setting up the neck as a skin-colored tube with a white collar ring made from a cylinder.

I'm adding cyborg details: a dark metal shoulder joint with a teal ring, a glowing chest port near the collarbone, and a mechanical left shin with darker metal coloring layered over the suit using color bands along the leg sweep.

For the left shin I'm swapping the white guard for exposed piston rods, and defining a subtle paint pattern for the suit material using a countershaded fill to give it panel-like shading variation.

I'm keeping the palette tight at around 16 flat colors to stay well under the 64-color limit, and applying a similar gentle countershade gradient to the white armor paint for a polished, painted look. I'm also planning decals—a chest emblem, shoulder stripes, and backpack panel lines—to add surface detail without adding geometry.

Now I'm sketching out the texture plan: eye and mouth textures, a backpack panel SVG with rivets and a teal cross, a cross emblem for chest and shoulder, and a glowing cyber forearm display with an ECG line for visual interest. I'm setting these up as textured plane parts oriented to face outward, using white as the base tint since the texture itself carries the color.

Working out the forearm screen's placement and orientation, computing a normal vector perpendicular to the arm's path direction so the display sits flush on the outer-top surface, then sizing and positioning it along the forearm with a slight glow. Now I'm defining the cyber forearm armor as metal rods swept along the arm path with a darker inner layer underneath.

Deciding to make the entire left arm mechanical, with a shoulder socket and dark metal bands tapering from shoulder to wrist, plus glowing teal rings at the elbow and wrist joints, and a large cyber hand with dark gray plating and a teal-lit knuckle. Starting to write the polyline code for the arm's path points.

Adding more shape helpers...

Writing imports and metadata...

Still defining countershaded colors... I realize I should drop the unused paint import, or actually use it for subtle panel-line detailing on the white suit sections instead.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton builder structure: creating hip, spine chain with three joints, and a neck chain of two joints connecting up to the head, parented appropriately so each limb can attach correctly later.

Adding jaw and arm joints...

Still building the leg chains and joint structure...

I need to handle the hand joint reference carefully for TS's flow analysis, declaring it outside the loop and checking it's defined before the staff logic uses it. Now I'm writing the torso loft with a series of width/height cross-sections at increasing heights to shape the body.

Adjusting the shoulder and chest station widths so the taper into the neck looks smooth under the collar, tweaking the final top station slightly smaller. Then I'm working out the bone binding for the loft -- associating hips and spine with the mesh and figuring out the closest-t clamping for where the hips joint sits relative to the loft start.

Keeping the accent sector stripes since they'll peek out at the waist and hips even though the chest plate covers most of them. Now I'm writing a helper function to generate elliptical belt rings via a sweep...

Setting up the belt's dimensions, buckle box with a glow inset, and hip pouches with flap details to flesh out the pelvis region.

I'll skip the yoke idea and instead handle shoulder armor via pauldrons. For the chest plate, I'm checking the z-depth alignment against the body loft at different heights to make sure the plate sits with a small, acceptable gap rather than clipping through — might need to lower the plate slightly to close that gap.

Below the chest I'm planning three small armor bands as flat boxes decreasing in width going down the abdomen, alternating white/suit colors, with a thin glowing accent strip centered on one of them. Then I'm starting on the pauldron shapes positioned symmetrically at the shoulders using ellipsoid forms.

For trim, I'm working out a ring band around the base of each pauldron, trying to pick a radius and direction that fits the dome shape without clearly knowing if it'll sit flush—considering a slightly larger radius so it doesn't clip inside the shoulder armor. Since that placement feels uncertain, I'm thinking of trying a second thin teal stripe instead as an alternative trim option.

I'm switching approach to a painted stripe directly on the pauldron surface using a conditional paint function that colors points near the z=0 plane with the accent color, nesting a white base paint underneath so it reads as a front-to-back stripe over the dome. For additional detail, I'm considering adding a small cross decal on the outer face of the pauldron, positioning a decal texture at the shoulder's outward-facing point sized to roughly match the curvature without distorting too much at the edges.

Next I'm thinking through the chest cross using simple glow boxes instead of a decal, and sketching the hip skirt plates/tassets as extruded polygon shapes with beveled edges, positioning them at the hip front and adding a small ellipsoid plate on the side for armor coverage. I'm also starting to plan a thigh holster cylinder for the outer leg.

Now I'm computing leg sweep radii and sketching the path points for hip, knee, and ankle positions on both legs, checking that the thigh geometry doesn't overlap near the crotch given the hip width and thigh radius.

For the leg color transition, I'm working out how to split suit color versus metal color along the sweep, considering whether to use a banded array or a simple color function that switches fill based on position along the leg.

I'm now mapping out the thigh guard geometry: picking rod radii that taper correctly against the leg's existing radius profile at the hip and knee points, plus adding a small teal accent band at the guard's lower edge where it meets the leg surface.

Adding leg sweep tubes with rounded ankle caps and boot overlays, a thigh holster for the s=-1 side, then defining ankle and toe joints with hinge roles for boot articulation, plus heel outline placement.

Adjusting the sole geometry to avoid z-fighting with the boot bottom, offsetting the boot slightly upward so the sole sits as a thin separate layer beneath it.

Adding boot details...

Settling on r.058 for the ellipsoid, then moving to the arms. For the left cyber arm I'm setting up a tapering chain radius across four points to shape the limb.

I'm adding a shoulder socket sphere with a teal ring, then deciding to make the left pauldron match the right in white with a cyber ring accent, plus thin piston rods running alongside the upper arm from shoulder to elbow.

Defining joint spheres and armor segments...

Checking the rod radius against a narrower screen width to keep the edges from floating too far off the surface, I'm considering switching to a flat-topped box frustum for the forearm to give the screen a clean mounting surface instead of a round tangent plane.

Still defining joint orientations... Now for the palm, I'll anchor it near the wrist joint, offset slightly along the hand's down direction. Then I move to the right arm, planning the suit sleeve color and armor rods for the upper arm guard and elbow.

Switching to finger setup for the cyber hand: metal sweep with rounded caps and thin radii, two joints per finger plus a two-joint thumb, giving ten joints per hand and twenty total. I'm tallying joint counts overall -- hips, spine, neck, jaw, and arms -- to get a running total for the skeleton.

Writing finger chain code...

Working out finger joint positions, computing each knuckle point as offsets along the direction and perpendicular vectors with varying finger lengths for index/middle/ring/pinky.

Now I'm setting up the thumb's start and joint points similarly, then sizing and orienting the palm box so its thickness runs roughly perpendicular to the hand's facing direction in the horizontal plane.

I'm defining the staff geometry next: a hinge joint attaching to the right hand, and a swept shaft running vertically at fixed x/z coordinates with a dark bluish-gray color.

Checking the color bands and grip positions along the staff, making sure the grip rod and ferrule segments don't collide with the finger placement.

Now I'm placing the orb at the pommel's top with a glowing core, then designing four cradle prongs that sweep outward and upward from the base to hold it in place.

I'm also adding tilted torus rings around the orb for an orbiting halo effect, sizing them to glow without clipping the prongs.

Now I'm sketching the wings extending from the collar, large sweeping shapes roughly .24 tall and .19 wide on each side, checking they clear the prong radius without overlapping awkwardly.

Realizing the prongs would be coplanar with the wings if left at 0/180 degrees, so I'm rotating them to 45/135/225/315 to avoid intersecting the wing plane. For the wing surface I'm considering a thin teal accent stripe along the bottom edge using a paint function that checks the extrude coordinate, switching between the white and accent colors.

Now moving to the backpack and head details -- defining skull and jaw geometry with skin-toned paint and a subtle countershade gradient for depth.

Nose, lips, and eyes come next using decals on a skull-plate surface, plus a partial-sphere cyber plate covering the left-front quadrant of the head, scaled and positioned to wrap around correctly and colored as metal.

Checking the plate's coverage: it does encompass the left eye region and extends down near the nose, creating a vertical boundary along the face centerline—essentially a hard-edged half-mask look similar to Overwatch-style cyborg characters like Genji.

I'm placing the organic eye decal on the right side and a mirrored cyber eye decal on the left plate, making sure raycasts pick up the outermost plate surface where they overlap. Then I'm sketching the hair geometry—a top cap using a partial sphere scaled and positioned near the crown, with a back cap piece still to define.

Still writing hair geometry...

Now I'm positioning the headset band to sit just outside the hair surface, sketching curve points that arc over the scalp from one side to the other at slightly varying heights and depths.

I'm placing cylindrical ear cups on either side of the head, white with glowing teal inner discs, and starting to think about where to attach a mic boom.

Now I'm sketching the mic boom with a curved path of segments down to a glowing tip, then shifting to the ponytail, building it as a chain of hair segments with a polyline path and checking it doesn't collide with the backpack top.

Placing canisters behind the pack with metal-capped cylinders, then figuring out where to fit a back panel texture in the gap between them on the pack's rear face.

For hoses, I'm sweeping a catmull curve from the pack side down toward a belt pouch, attaching it to a spine bone, and mirroring it on both sides for symmetry. Still need to handle the neck collar and left-side neck cables, plus a thin teal glow element.

For the chest I'll skip a left cyber port and instead add two vertical glow strips on the chest plate edges with a small teal cross centered at the sternum, checking that the strip and cross dimensions don't overlap awkwardly.

I still want to add left leg piston details, knee actuators, hip pouches, and a vial before writing the final code. I'm defining a small helper function that wraps the extrude call for plates, passing through position, thickness, color, bevel, and bone binding so I can reuse it for each armor piece, and confirming the bevel logic caps correctly at half the thickness when needed.

Setting up more helpers now — checking that joint chains expose a usable Joint array, writing a band helper that accepts either tuple vectors or THREE.Vector3 inputs by normalizing with an instanceof check, and wrapping sweep calls with sensible defaults like six-sided tubes. I'm also sketching an ellipsoid helper built on a sphere geometry with configurable radii, tessellation detail, position, and bone binding for reuse across body parts.

Now I'm drafting cylinder and box helper wrappers, a glow utility for part emphasis, and starting an SVG design for the eye — sketching eyebrow and almond-shaped eye paths, iris circle, and pupil within a small viewBox so proportions stay consistent across uses.

Still designing eye textures...

Checking the jaw sphere geometry, I realize it's the outermost surface near the mouth, so the mouth decal needs to target the combined skull/plate/jaw surface rather than just the skull, since the jaw part extends further at that y-range.

For the cross icon texture, I'm sketching a rounded plus-sign shape made from two overlapping rectangles in teal, with a white stroke outline to give it some contrast against the background.

Now I'm designing the panel texture for the pack side: a light rounded base panel with grey border lines, rivet circles, a small teal cross at the top, and dark horizontal slits, sized for a tall narrow aspect ratio with appropriately scaled stroke widths. I'm also starting on the screen texture, picking a dark base color for its viewBox.

Writing ECG polyline path...

Adding mechanical details to the legs now: knee actuator rods, piston details for the left leg, teal-banded guards on the shins, calf vents, and a thigh holster with an injector box on the right side.

I'm linking the pauldron to the shoulder joint so it rotates naturally with the arm, adding an elbow pad ellipsoid offset slightly behind the joint, and setting up a polyline helper for the arm points before starting the export code.

Writing builder function and spine joint destructuring...

Still writing character geometry...

Still writing arm chain code...

Writing finger wrap geometry...

Adding thumb joints, left-hand fingers, and double-checking parenting order for the staff and limb joints before writing the full file, including naming checks for head, neck, jaw, hand tips, and tasset outlines on the hips.

Writing boot outline and sole plates...

I'm checking that the sole bottom sits exactly at y=0, and that the ankle/shin boot geometry properly conceals the joint sweep. I'm also confirming type usages like OutlinePoint, PartOptions, Paint, and Joint are all correctly wired, before moving on to placing the bandolier vial rings.

The bandolier ring dimensions don't quite match the torso's taper — at the strap's y-range the torso half-width is narrower than my rx value, making it float outside the body. I'm adjusting rx and rz smaller so the strap hugs the chest more closely across its vertical span.

Still placing vials and belt pouch boxes...
